info.title: iSnap API
info.description: The iSnap API sends and receives iMessage, RCS and SMS on real phone lines, manages those lines, and reports events through webhooks. Every message is sent to a real recipient, with an `isnap_live_` key and with an `isnap_test_` key alike. Retry a `429` after `Retry-After` seconds. Retry a `500` or a `503` up to 2 times, with exponential backoff. Do not retry any other `4xx`: fix the request. Retry a write only on an operation that honors `Idempotency-Key`, with the key of the first attempt. Responses carry personal data: handles, names and message text.

bearerAuth.description: An API key created in the iSnap dashboard, or a trial key, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. An API key starts with `isnap_live_` or `isnap_test_`; both act on the same account, lines and billing. A trial key acts on its trial only.

checks.description: One entry per dependency of the API. Each value is `ok` or `error`.

HealthResponse.description: The health of the API. This body is returned as is, without the standard envelope.

status.description: The HTTP status of the response.

code.description: Stable machine-readable code that names the refusal. Branch on this value.

message.description: Text for a person. It can change between versions: do not branch on it.

retry_after.description: Seconds to wait before the next attempt. Set on the `429` responses that know a delay, where the `Retry-After` header carries the same value. When it is above 60 seconds, do not wait in a request: schedule the call, or report the time. `null` on every other error.

retry_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp at which the refusal ends. Set only on `429 rebind_cap_reached`. `null` on every other error.

path.description: Where the problem is: the field names and array indexes that lead to it.

code.description: Kind of problem. On `validation_failed`, for example `invalid_type`, `invalid_value`, `invalid_format`, `invalid_union`, `invalid_key`, `invalid_element`, `too_small`, `too_big`, `not_multiple_of`, `unrecognized_keys` or `custom`. The list is open: read `path` and `message`.

min.description: Smallest accepted value. Present only on `limit_out_of_bounds`, `mac_quantity_not_a_pack`, `byop_reduction_strands_mac_sessions` and `byop_reduction_strands_byod_lines`.

max.description: Largest accepted value. Present only on `limit_out_of_bounds` and `mac_sessions_exceed_byop_lines`, and on the `too_big` issue of an `Idempotency-Key` header longer than 255 characters.

issues.description: Problems found in the request, one entry each. Set on most `400 validation_failed` responses and on the refusals that name a field: a refused `handle` of `POST /v1/lookup` has `issues: null`. `null` on every other error.

error.description: What went wrong. The six fields are always present; `retry_after`, `retry_at` and `issues` are `null` when they do not apply.

request_id.description: Id of the request that produced this response: `req_` followed by 25 letters or digits.

ErrorEnvelope.description: The body of an error response.

version.description: The version of the API: three numbers separated by dots. The same value as `info.version` in the OpenAPI document.

trace_id.description: Trace id of the request that produced this response: 32 lowercase hexadecimal characters. Quote it when you report a problem to iSnap.

request_id.description: Id of the request that produced this response: `req_` followed by 25 letters or digits.

id.description: Id of a line: `line_` followed by 25 letters or digits.

phone_number.description: The phone number of the line in E.164 format. An empty string, never `null`, when the line has no number: a BYOD line whose device has not reported one, or a shared line. `GET /v1/attention` returns `null` for such a line. Masked on `GET /v1/lines`, and on `GET /v1/lines/{id}` unless the caller owns the line: `+1 (AAA) ***-**DD` for a North American number, the country code, asterisks and the last two digits for any other number.

area_code.description: The 3-digit North American area code of the number. `null` for any other number, and while the number is not known.

country_code.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country of the number. `null` while the number is not known.

state.description: Two-letter code of the US state the area code belongs to. `null` outside the US, and while the number is not known.

state_name.description: Name of that US state, for example `California`. `null` whenever `state` is `null`.

billing_tier.description: The kind of line. `rental_iphone`: a rented line that sends iMessage and SMS. `rental_android`: a rented line that sends SMS and RCS. `byod_imessage`: a BYOD line on your own Mac and iPhone. `byod_android`: a BYOD line on your own Android phone. `shared_imessage`: a shared line. `shared_pool`: a test line when `test_line` is `true`, otherwise a dedicated pool line: a line of iSnap that is dedicated to your account.

byod.description: `true` for a BYOD line, which runs on your own device: `billing_tier` is `byod_imessage` or `byod_android`.

inbound_only.description: `true` for an inbound-only line: it can message a contact only after that contact has messaged it. A send to any other handle returns `403 outbound_first_forbidden`. Only a rented line can be inbound-only: always `false` on BYOD, shared and test lines.

capabilities.description: The services the line sends, as an array of lowercase names: `["imessage", "sms"]` on `rental_iphone` and `byod_imessage` lines, `["sms", "rcs"]` on `rental_android` and `byod_android` lines, `["imessage"]` on a shared line. A test line that you made from a rented line keeps the array of that line. On a dedicated pool line, and on a test line that iSnap created for your account, the array does not tell the services and can be `["sms"]`: such a line is an iMessage line.

status.description: One of six values. `provisioning`: the line is being prepared for one of your pre-orders. `available`: the line belongs to no account and can be reserved or assigned. `reserved`: the line is reserved for one account until `expires_at`; it is not billed and cannot send. `active`: the line belongs to its owner; it is the only status in which a line sends. `suspended`: the line still belongs to its owner but cannot send (`403 line_suspended`); a line billed by a per-line subscription is suspended when a payment for it fails, iSnap can also suspend a line, and no API operation ends a suspension. `cancelled`: the line is ended for good and keeps its owner.

monthly_price.description: Deprecated. Catalog price of this kind of line, in US cents. It is not the amount billed for the line. Removed in the next major version: no removal date is set.

stripe_subscription_id.description: Id of the per-line subscription that bills the line. `null` on a line billed on the monthly wholesale invoice, on BYOD, shared and test lines, and on a rented line that a direct account received by transfer while the line was not `active`.

activated_at.description: Timestamp at which the line became `active` (ISO 8601, UTC). `null` on a line that was never activated, and again on a line that returned to the marketplace. A transfer to a wholesale partner sets it to the time of the transfer; a transfer to a direct account keeps the earlier value.

expires_at.description: End of the reservation (ISO 8601, UTC): 15 minutes after the line was reserved. Read it only while `status` is `reserved`: in any other status it is `null` or a past timestamp.

anniversary_at.description: The anniversary of the line: the timestamp at which you took it (ISO 8601, UTC). `POST /v1/lines/{id}/cancel` ends the line at the next occurrence of this timestamp. iSnap sets it each time a line becomes a wholesale partner's, a transfer included, and `POST /v1/lines/{id}/anniversary` replaces it. A conversion to a test line and back keeps it. `null` on a line owned by a direct account or by no account, and on a line of a wholesale partner whose anniversary was never set.

cancel_at.description: Timestamp at which iSnap ends this line (ISO 8601, UTC). Set by `POST /v1/lines/{id}/cancel` and cleared by `POST /v1/lines/{id}/uncancel`. The line works and is billed as before until then. `null` when no end is scheduled. A line that ended at this date keeps the value. On a test line ended with `POST /v1/lines/{id}/terminate`, it holds the time the line ended.

billing_anchor_at.description: The billing anchor you stated for this line (ISO 8601, UTC): a line billed on the monthly wholesale invoice is billed at each monthly occurrence of this timestamp. `null` when you stated none: the line is then billed at each monthly occurrence of `activated_at`. State it with `POST /v1/pre-orders`, `POST /v1/lines/{id}/activate` or `PATCH /v1/lines/{id}`. A change applies from the next occurrence and does not alter a month already billed.

next_anchor_at.description: For a line billed on the monthly wholesale invoice: the next timestamp at which it is billed (ISO 8601, UTC). It is the next occurrence, strictly after the read, of `billing_anchor_at`, or of `activated_at` when no billing anchor is stated: the same day of the month, moved to the last day of a shorter month, at the same time of day. `null` when the line is not `active` or `suspended`, when it was never activated, and when its `cancel_at` falls on or before that occurrence. A line billed by a per-line subscription also carries a value here, which does not tell when that line is billed.

inbound_only.description: The value `inbound_only` takes when the change applies.

effective_at.description: The billing anchor occurrence at which the change applies (ISO 8601, UTC). iSnap applies it after this timestamp, and before it charges the line for the month that starts then: the API does not bound the delay.

pending_variant.description: The variant change scheduled for this line, or `null` when none is pending. The `inbound_only` field of the line keeps its value until the change applies. Schedule a change with `POST /v1/lines/{id}/variant` and `effective: "next_anchor"`; withdraw it with `DELETE /v1/lines/{id}/variant`. It becomes `null` when the change is applied, when it is withdrawn, when it can no longer apply at its date, when the line becomes a test line, and when the line leaves its owner without ending. A line that ends keeps its `pending_variant`, and the change never applies.

created_at.description: Timestamp at which iSnap created the line (ISO 8601, UTC). It is not the date you acquired the line.

metadata.description: Your own key-value data on the line. `null` when the line has none. A line created with `"metadata": {}` reads `{}`: treat `null` and `{}` the same. It is part of the line object for every caller, `GET /v1/lines` and `GET /v1/lines/{id}` included, and a line that returns to the marketplace keeps it: never put personal data or secrets in it.

test_line.description: `true` for a test line: a line you set aside to host the trials of your own prospects. Its `billing_tier` is `shared_pool`.

shared.description: `true` for a shared line, which has no device and no phone number of its own: its `billing_tier` is `shared_imessage` and its `phone_number` is an empty string.

fulfillment_status.description: Present only on `GET /v1/lines/my`. `open` while an order for this line is still being fulfilled, `null` otherwise.

Line.description: A line. `billing_tier`, `byod`, `shared`, `test_line` and `inbound_only` tell the kinds of line apart: a rented line (two-way or inbound-only), a BYOD line, a shared line, a test line.

id.description: Id of the hosted macOS session: `mcs_` followed by 25 letters or digits. Keep it: no operation lists sessions.

rented.description: `true` on every session you can read: once a session is released, every operation on it returns `404`.

anniversary_at.description: Start of the rental. The session is billed every month on the day of the month of this timestamp, in UTC, at the same time of day; in a shorter month, on its last day. Never `null` on a session you can read.

cancel_at.description: End of the rental when a cancellation is scheduled: the next occurrence of `anniversary_at` strictly after the cancel call. The session works and is billed until then. `null` when no cancellation is scheduled.

status.description: `created`: the Mac that hosts the session is delivered. `pending_provisioning`: iSnap marked that Mac as not delivered. A session is rented out on a delivered Mac only, so `pending_provisioning` appears only when the mark changes after the rental started.

created_at.description: Timestamp at which iSnap created the session. It can be earlier than the start of your rental, which is `anniversary_at`.

metadata.description: Your metadata on the rental, set with `POST /v1/macos-sessions/rent` or `PATCH /v1/macos-sessions/{id}`, and sent as `data.metadata` on the `macos_session.*` events. `null` when the rental has none. Cleared when the session is released.

MacosSession.description: A hosted macOS session that the account rents.

lines.description: One page of available lines, ordered by `area_code` then `phone_number`, with masked phone numbers.

total.description: Number of lines that match the filters, across all pages.

lines.description: Your lines whose `status` is `active` or `reserved`, ordered by `created_at`, oldest first, with full phone numbers.

MyLines.description: The lines of your account that are `active` or `reserved`.

billing_tier.description: The kind of line to take.

area_code.description: Take a line whose `area_code` is exactly this value. Omit it to take a line of any area code.

inbound_only.description: `true` to take the line as an inbound-only line. Rented tiers only (`400 inbound_only_not_rental` otherwise). Defaults to `false`: a two-way line.

as_test_line.description: `true` to make the line a test line for the trials of your own prospects, in the same call. Rented tiers only (`400 test_line_not_rental` otherwise), and not together with `inbound_only` (`400 test_line_not_inbound_only`). Defaults to `false`.

metadata.description: Your own key-value data, set on the line in place of any `metadata` it carried. Omit it to clear the `metadata` of the line. At most 20 keys and 8,192 bytes once serialized as JSON. The keys `migration_ref` and `proof_line` are reserved (`400 reserved_metadata_key`). Never put personal data or secrets in it.

AssignLine.description: The line to take: its kind and, optionally, its area code, its variant and its `metadata`.

metadata.description: Your own key-value data, set on the new line. At most 20 keys and 8,192 bytes once serialized as JSON. The keys `migration_ref` and `proof_line` are reserved (`400 reserved_metadata_key`). Never put personal data or secrets in it.

MintSharedLine.description: Optional `metadata` for the new shared line.

inbound_only.description: `true` to activate the line as an inbound-only line. Rented lines only (`400 inbound_only_not_rental` otherwise). Defaults to `false`: a two-way line.

billing_anchor_at.description: The billing anchor of the line: an ISO 8601 timestamp in UTC, with a `Z` suffix. A line billed on the monthly wholesale invoice is charged one full month at each monthly occurrence of this timestamp: the same day of the month, moved to the last day of a shorter month, at the same time of day. At the first occurrence after its activation, the line is also credited for the days that the month charged at activation had already paid for past that occurrence. Omit it to bill the line at each monthly occurrence of its activation. A past timestamp is accepted. A timestamp more than 31 days after the request returns `400 billing_anchor_too_far`.

ActivateLine.description: Optional settings of the activated line: its variant and its billing anchor.

to_user_id.description: UUID of the iSnap account that receives the line. An unknown account returns `400 invalid_recipient`.

preserve_device_session.description: Defaults to `true`: the device of the line stays connected and the line keeps working for the new owner. `false` revokes the device sessions of the line, so the device must be paired again.

TransferOwnership.description: The account that receives the line, and what happens to the device sessions of the line.

inbound_only.description: `true` for the inbound-only variant: the line can message a contact only after that contact has messaged it. `false` for the two-way variant.

effective.description: When the change applies. `now`, the default: immediately, so the next send obeys the new value. `next_anchor`: at a billing anchor occurrence of the line; until then `inbound_only` keeps its value and `pending_variant` holds the change. An immediate change does not withdraw a scheduled one: use `DELETE /v1/lines/{id}/variant` for that.

not_before.description: Used only with `effective: "next_anchor"`; ignored otherwise. The earliest timestamp at which the change can apply (ISO 8601, UTC, with a `Z` suffix). The change applies at the first billing anchor occurrence at or after it, returned as `pending_variant.effective_at`. Defaults to the time of the request. A past timestamp returns `400 not_before_in_the_past`.

SetLineVariant.description: The variant to give the line, and when the change applies. A field that the body does not declare is ignored: a misspelled `effective` applies the change immediately.

reason.description: Optional note of 1 to 255 characters, with no control character. Returned as `reason` in the `line.terminated` event. Defaults to `terminated by the customer`.

TerminateLine.description: An optional note for the termination.

anniversary_at.description: The timestamp at which you took this line (ISO 8601, UTC, with a `Z` suffix). The day of the month and the time of day are both kept. A future timestamp returns `400 anniversary_in_the_future`.

SetLineAnniversary.description: The anniversary to record on the line.

metadata.description: Keys to merge into the `metadata` of the line: a key with a value is set, a key with `null` is removed, a key you do not send is kept. The result holds at most 20 keys and 8,192 bytes once serialized as JSON (`400 metadata_too_large`); a request that only removes keys is never refused for the size of the result. The keys `migration_ref` and `proof_line` are reserved (`400 reserved_metadata_key`). Never put personal data or secrets in it.

billing_anchor_at.description: The billing anchor of the line: an ISO 8601 timestamp in UTC, with a `Z` suffix, or `null` to clear it. A line billed on the monthly wholesale invoice is charged one full month at each monthly occurrence of this timestamp: the same day of the month, moved to the last day of a shorter month, at the same time of day. Without a billing anchor, the line is billed at each monthly occurrence of its activation. A change applies from the next occurrence and does not alter a month already billed. A past timestamp is accepted. A timestamp more than 31 days after the request returns `400 billing_anchor_too_far`. Sending the value the line already has changes nothing.

daily_total_frees_at.description: Timestamp at which `daily_messages_used` drops back under its limit (ISO 8601, UTC). `null` when the counter is under its limit, when the limit is 0, or when the time is not known: read `null` as no known wait.

daily_new_frees_at.description: Timestamp at which `daily_new_contacts_used` drops back under its limit (ISO 8601, UTC). `null` when the counter is under its limit, when the limit is 0, or when the time is not known: read `null` as no known wait.

daily_known_frees_at.description: Timestamp at which `daily_known_contacts_used` drops back under its limit (ISO 8601, UTC). `null` when the counter is under its limit, when the limit is 0, or when the time is not known: read `null` as no known wait.

QuotaSnapshot.description: The sending limits of a line with their counters. Every counter covers a rolling window.

new_contacts_at_80_percent.description: `true` when `daily_new_contacts_used` is at 80% of `daily_new_contact_limit` or more.

known_contacts_at_80_percent.description: `true` when `daily_known_contacts_used` is at 80% of `daily_known_contact_limit` or more.

messages_at_80_percent.description: `true` when `daily_messages_used` is at 80% of `daily_total_message_limit` or more.

hourly_at_80_percent.description: `true` when `hourly_messages_used` is at 80% of `hourly_message_limit` or more.

minute_at_80_percent.description: `true` when `minute_messages_used` is at 80% of `minute_message_limit` or more.

BucketsWarning.description: One flag per sending limit: `true` from 80% of the limit. A flag is `false` when its limit is 0.

QueueSummary.description: Totals of the queue of the line, and its sending limits with their counters.

id.description: Id of the message: `msg_` followed by 25 letters or digits.

to.description: The recipient of the message. Personal data.

body.description: The text of the message. `null` or an empty string when the message has no text. Personal data.

status.description: `scheduled`: iSnap holds the message until `scheduled_for`. `queued`: the message waits for the device of the line, or the device has it and has not confirmed the send. `delivered_to_device`: the device confirmed the send (the message `status` is `sent`) and no delivery receipt has arrived; such an item stays listed until a receipt arrives or the message is deleted.

scheduled_for.description: Planned send time of a held message (ISO 8601, UTC). For a message that is not held, the time it entered the queue.

schedule_reason.description: Why the message is held: `minute_limit_exceeded`, `hourly_limit_exceeded`, `total_message_quota_exceeded`, `new_contact_quota_exceeded`, `known_contact_quota_exceeded`, `inter_message_delay`, `inter_new_contact_delay`, `quiet_hours`, `carrier_retry` or `pending_retry`; ignore values you do not know. `null` on a message that is not held.

queue_position.description: Rank of the item in the returned order, starting at 1 and counting the items of earlier pages.

is_new_contact.description: Whether the recipient counted as a new contact when the message was accepted or released. `null` when not known.

target_activity_hour.description: The hour of `scheduled_for`, from 0 to 23, read in `timezone`. `null` when the message has no planned send time.

timezone.description: IANA time zone `target_activity_hour` is read in: the time zone of the recipient when iSnap knows it, otherwise the time zone of the line.

created_at.description: Timestamp at which iSnap recorded the message (ISO 8601, UTC).

QueueItem.description: One outbound message of the line that is held, waiting for the device, or sent and not yet reported delivered.

trace_id.description: Trace id of the request that produced this response: 32 lowercase hexadecimal characters. Quote it when you report a problem to iSnap.

request_id.description: Id of the request that produced this response: `req_` followed by 25 letters or digits.

line_id.description: Id of a line: `line_` followed by 25 letters or digits.

byod.description: Always `true`: this operation serves BYOD lines only.

state.description: `offline`: the device of the line has not reported for 5 minutes or more, or has not reported since it was paired, and the line was not already `degraded` by its reception checks. `degraded`: the line fails its reception checks, or its device reports with a `send_text` capability (and, on an iMessage line, an `imessage` capability) that is not `active`. A line that is `degraded` because its reception checks fail stays `degraded` when its device stops reporting: read `last_heartbeat_at`. `active`: neither applies.

last_heartbeat_at.description: Timestamp of the last report of the paired device (ISO 8601, UTC). `null` when the line has no active device session, or when the device has never reported.

daily_quota_remaining.description: The smallest room left among the three 24-hour sending limits of the line: new contacts, known contacts and messages. Never below 0.

apple_id_flagged.description: `true` once the device has reported that Apple disabled or challenged the Apple ID of the line. `line.apple_id_flagged` is sent when it becomes `true`. Only iSnap sets it back to `false`, and no event announces that.

last_error.description: Free text of at most 1,000 characters, or `null` when the line has no error: the reason reported with an Apple ID flag, the comma-separated reasons of a line that fails its reception checks, among `apple_account_reauth_required`, `phone_alias_unregistered` and `not_receiving`, or the text reported for the last message that failed. It is cleared when the line recovers from an `offline` or `degraded` state and when iSnap clears the Apple ID flag, so it can hold a message failure while `state` is `active`. Do not treat it as a fixed list of values.

last_offline_at.description: Timestamp at which the most recent offline period started (ISO 8601, UTC). Kept after the line recovers. `null` when the line has never been offline.

bridge_version.description: Version of the bridge app that runs on the paired device. `null` when the line has no active device session, or when the device has not reported it.

runtime_capabilities.description: What the device can do, as it last reported: one entry per capability, each `active`, `degraded` or `disabled`. The capabilities reported are `imessage`, `sms_fallback`, `send_text`, `send_attachment`, `reactions_out`, `reaction_remove_out`, `mark_read_out`, `typing_out`, `effects`, `reactions_in`, `read_receipts_in`, `typing_in` and `lookup_probe`; ignore the ones you do not know. `null` when the line has no active device session, or when the device has not reported any.

device_state.description: The state the device last reported about itself, independent of `state`: `online`, `degraded`, `offline`, `initializing` or `blocked`. `null` when the line has no active device session, or when the device has not reported it.

storage_free_bytes.description: Free storage on the device, in bytes, as last reported. `null` means not reported, not zero.

It depends on whether the line is an iMessage line or an Android line, and iSnap can change it: read it here instead of storing it. Send it as `activity_curve` in `PATCH /v1/lines/{id}/config` to remove the override.

timezone.description: IANA time zone of the line. Without an override, iSnap derives it from the North American area code of the line, else from its country when that country has a single time zone; otherwise it is `Europe/London` for a `+44` number and `America/Chicago` for any other number.

hour.description: Hour of the day, from 0 to 23, in the local time of the recipient.

weight.description: Weight of this hour, a non-negative integer. 0 makes it a quiet hour; a larger weight gives the hour a larger share of the held messages.

EffectiveLineConfig.description: The value in force for every key of the configuration: the override of the line where it has one, the default otherwise.

LineConfigKnobs.description: The eight limits that have a default and bounds: the five message limits and the three reply limits. Each has its value in force, its default and its bounds `min` and `max`. A value above `default` is accepted only for the five message limits of a BYOD line, up to `max`.

current.description: The value in force on the line.

default.description: The default value. It depends on whether the line is an iMessage line or an Android line, and iSnap can change it.

min.description: The smallest value the API accepts for this key.

max.description: The upper bound of this key. A value above `default` is accepted, up to `max`, only on a BYOD line and only for `daily_new_contact_limit`, `daily_known_contact_limit`, `daily_total_message_limit`, `hourly_message_limit` and `minute_message_limit`. On any other line, and for the three reply limits on every line, a value above `default` returns `403 cannot_increase_limit`. A value above `max` is refused first, on every line, with `422 limit_out_of_bounds` or `400 validation_failed`.

LineConfigKnobBounds.description: One limit of the line: the value in force, its default, and its bounds. A value above the default is accepted only for the five message limits of a BYOD line.

default_use_typing_indicator.description: Whether a message that does not state `use_typing_indicator` shows the typing indicator before it is sent.

quota_overflow_behavior.description: What happens to a send that reaches a sending limit. `queue`: the message is accepted and held, with `status: scheduled`. `drop` or `fail`: the send returns `429` and nothing is stored; the two values behave the same.

daily_new_contact_limit.description: Distinct new contacts the line can message per rolling 24 hours. Accepted values: 5 to 200. Another integer from 1 to 500 returns `422 limit_out_of_bounds`. A value outside 1 to 500, or one that is not an integer, returns `400 validation_failed`. It can only be lowered below the default (`403 cannot_increase_limit`), except on a BYOD line, where it can be raised up to `knobs.daily_new_contact_limit.max`.

daily_known_contact_limit.description: Distinct known contacts the line can message per rolling 24 hours. Accepted values: 10 to 1,000. Another integer from 1 to 2,000 returns `422 limit_out_of_bounds`. A value outside 1 to 2,000, or one that is not an integer, returns `400 validation_failed`. It can only be lowered below the default (`403 cannot_increase_limit`), except on a BYOD line, where it can be raised up to `knobs.daily_known_contact_limit.max`.

daily_total_message_limit.description: Messages the line can send per rolling 24 hours. Accepted values: 10 to 1,000. Another integer from 1 to 100,000 returns `422 limit_out_of_bounds`. A value outside 1 to 100,000, or one that is not an integer, returns `400 validation_failed`. It can only be lowered below the default (`403 cannot_increase_limit`), except on a BYOD line, where it can be raised up to `knobs.daily_total_message_limit.max`.

hourly_message_limit.description: Messages the line can send per rolling 60 minutes. Accepted values: 5 to 200. Another integer from 1 to 1,000 returns `422 limit_out_of_bounds`. A value outside 1 to 1,000, or one that is not an integer, returns `400 validation_failed`. It can only be lowered below the default (`403 cannot_increase_limit`), except on a BYOD line, where it can be raised up to `knobs.hourly_message_limit.max`.

minute_message_limit.description: Messages the line can send per rolling 60 seconds. Accepted values: 1 to 60. An integer from 61 to 100 returns `422 limit_out_of_bounds`. A value outside 1 to 100, or one that is not an integer, returns `400 validation_failed`. It can only be lowered below the default (`403 cannot_increase_limit`), except on a BYOD line, where it can be raised up to `knobs.minute_message_limit.max`.

min_inter_message_seconds.description: Minimum number of seconds between two messages of the line. Accepted values: 1 to 300. It can only be raised above the default (`403 cannot_decrease_delay`).

min_inter_new_contact_seconds.description: Minimum number of seconds between two first messages to new contacts. Accepted values: 30 to 3,600. It can only be raised above the default (`403 cannot_decrease_delay`).

max_queue_depth.description: Maximum number of held messages on the line: beyond it, a send that would be held returns `429 queue_full`. Accepted values: 10 to 5,000. It can only be lowered below the default (`403 cannot_increase_limit`).

reply_window_hours.description: Reply lane: a message qualifies as a reply when its recipient messaged the line within this number of hours. Accepted values: 1 to 168. It can only be lowered below the default (`403 cannot_increase_limit`).

reply_max_per_inbound.description: Reply lane: the number of messages to a contact that qualify as replies after each message from that contact. 0 turns the reply lane off. Accepted values: 0 to 50. It can only be lowered below the default (`403 cannot_increase_limit`).

daily_reply_limit.description: Reply-lane allowance: the number of replies per rolling 24 hours that can pass a sending limit through the reply lane. 0 turns the reply lane off. Accepted values: 0 to 1,000. It can only be lowered below the default (`403 cannot_increase_limit`).

timezone.description: IANA time zone name of the line, for example `America/New_York` (`400 validation_failed` otherwise). iSnap reads quiet hours in it for a recipient whose own time zone it does not know. Once set, it can be replaced but not removed.

hour.description: Hour of the day, from 0 to 23, in the local time of the recipient.

weight.description: Weight of this hour, a non-negative integer. 0 makes it a quiet hour; a larger weight gives the hour a larger share of the held messages.

activity_curve.description: The sending hours of the line, as a list of hours with a weight. An hour with weight 0, or with no entry, is a quiet hour: a message accepted then is held until the next hour that has a weight. Messages held by a 24-hour sending limit are placed in the hours in proportion to their weights. It needs at least one entry, no hour twice, and a total weight above 0 (`422 invalid_activity_curve` otherwise). A curve the same as `default_activity_curve` (returned by `GET /v1/lines/{id}/config`) removes the override instead of setting one. Two curves are the same when every hour from 0 to 23 has the same weight in both, an hour with no entry counting as 0: the order of the entries does not matter, and a curve that lists only its weighted hours is the same as the 24-hour curve with 0 everywhere else.

LineConfigPatch.description: The keys to override on this line. Send a key with its default value to remove its override. `null` and unknown keys return `400 validation_failed`.

preferred_area_codes.description: The area codes you listed, in order of preference.

inbound_only.description: `true` for an inbound-only line, `false` for a two-way line.

billing_anchor_at.description: The billing anchor you set when creating the pre-order, carried onto the line when the line is created. `null` when you set none.

stripe_client_secret.description: Client secret for the payment form of Stripe, to collect the first month. Set only in the response of `POST /v1/pre-orders/{id}/confirm`, when that response carries the pre-order in status `awaiting_payment`: the first time and every time confirm is repeated. `null` in every other response.

estimated_fulfillment.description: Estimated time of the hand-over of the line: the time the build starts plus 72 hours. Set once, when the build starts, and never revised. `null` while the pre-order is `draft` or `awaiting_payment`, and on a pre-order canceled before its build started.

created_at.description: Timestamp of creation, ISO 8601 in UTC.

updated_at.description: Timestamp of the last change of the pre-order, ISO 8601 in UTC.

metadata.description: Your metadata on the pre-order, set at creation or with `PATCH /v1/pre-orders/{id}`, and sent as `data.metadata` on every `pre_order.*` event. `null` when the pre-order has none. It is not copied onto the line that the pre-order produces.

PreOrder.description: A pre-order: an order for one rented iMessage line.

PreOrderStatus.description: `draft`: created, with no effect. `awaiting_payment`: confirmed by a direct account, and the first month is due; nothing is built until it is paid. `provisioning`: the build has started, and the line is being prepared. `fulfilled`: the line is handed over. `cancelled`: the pre-order ended with no line. You canceled it, its first month was not paid within 23 hours of the confirmation, or its subscription was canceled before the first payment. A pre-order whose build has started never becomes `cancelled`.

DeviceFulfillmentStatus.description: Progress of the line. `awaiting_hardware`: the line is not ready; also the value of a pre-order that has no line: a draft, a pre-order in `awaiting_payment`, a canceled pre-order. `ready`: the line is prepared. `deployed`: the line is handed over. `received` and `setup_in_progress` are declared and never returned. Always present on a pre-order, and never `null`.

next_cursor.description: Cursor of the next page when `has_more` is `true`, otherwise `null`. Send it as `cursor`.

request_id.description: Id of the request that produced this response: `req_` followed by 25 letters or digits.

metadata.description: Keys to merge into the metadata of the pre-order. A key with a value is set, and a key with `null` is deleted. At most 20 keys and 8,192 bytes once serialized as JSON.

PatchPreOrder.description: Metadata to merge into the metadata of a pre-order.

trace_id.description: Trace id of the request that produced this response: 32 lowercase hexadecimal characters. Quote it when you report a problem to iSnap.

request_id.description: Id of the request that produced this response: `req_` followed by 25 letters or digits.

id.description: Message id: `msg_` followed by 25 letters or digits.

line_id.description: Id of the line that sent or received the message.

to.description: On an outbound message sent through the API, the recipient's phone number in E.164. On a message typed on the line's device, the contact's handle as the device reports it. On an inbound message, the line's number: on a shared line, the number that serves the contact. A contact's number is personal data.

from.description: On an outbound message, the line's number: an empty string when the line has no number, and on a shared line the number that serves the contact. On an inbound message, the sender's handle, a phone number or an email address of up to 255 characters: exactly as the line's device stores it, without normalization, or normalized on a shared line (E.164 for a phone number). A phone number can come in another form than E.164: before you compare it with a number you send to, bring both to E.164. A contact's handle is personal data.

body.description: Text of the message. `null` when the message has no text: a message with attachments only, or a reaction. The text of an inbound message is cut to 10,000 characters.

oneOf.description: A bubble effect: an effect on the message bubble.
A screen effect: a full-screen effect.

effect.description: The iMessage effect of the message, or `null` when it has none. On an outbound message, the effect you sent. On an inbound message, the effect the sender used, when the line's device reports it.

reply_to_message_id.description: Id of the message this message replies to, or `null`. It becomes `null` when iSnap deletes the message replied to.

use_typing_indicator.description: On an outbound message, whether the line's device shows the typing indicator to the recipient before it sends the message. A message sent with an API key on a line that is not an iMessage line always has `false`. It has no meaning on an inbound message.

metadata.description: The `metadata` you sent with the message, unchanged. `null` when you sent none, and on an inbound message.

attachments.description: The files of the message, in order. Empty when the message has none. Files received with an inbound message are listed here too.

reactions.description: The reactions on the message, at most one per author. Empty when the message has none, and always empty on an entry whose `kind` is `reaction`. The line's own reaction appears as soon as the API accepts it, and disappears as soon as the API accepts its removal, before the line's device confirms either. It stays listed when the device fails to place it.

scheduled_for.description: On a held message (`status: scheduled`), the planned departure time. On an outbound message that was not held, or that has left its hold, the same value as `queued_at`: read `sent_at` for the time the message was sent. `null` on an inbound message and on a message typed on the device of the line.

schedule_reason.description: Why iSnap holds the message, while its `status` is `scheduled`. `minute_limit_exceeded`, `hourly_limit_exceeded`, `total_message_quota_exceeded`, `new_contact_quota_exceeded` or `known_contact_quota_exceeded`: a sending limit of the line is reached. `inter_message_delay` or `inter_new_contact_delay`: the spacing between two messages of the line. `quiet_hours`: the message was accepted outside the line's sending hours, counted in the recipient's local time. `carrier_retry`: on a shared line, the number that serves the contact is busy or offline. `pending_retry`: iSnap is retrying the release. A message held behind an earlier message to the same recipient takes the `schedule_reason` of that earlier message while the earlier one is held, and `inter_message_delay` (`carrier_retry` on a shared line) while the earlier one waits for the line's device: `schedule_reason` alone does not tell you that a message waits for an earlier one. `null` on a message that was never held, and `null` again once the message is released. Treat a value you do not know as a hold: more values can be added.

reply_lane.description: `true` when the message is in the reply lane: it answers a contact who wrote to the line in the last 24 hours, within the limits of the reply lane. Such a message is not held by the hourly limit, by the three 24-hour limits or by quiet hours. Set when the message is accepted. A held message enters the reply lane when its contact writes to the line while it waits, whatever held it, oldest first and within the same limits: the value then changes from `false` to `true`, once and never back, and the message is released without waiting for its `scheduled_for`, still after the earlier messages to the same recipient and within the per-minute limit and the spacing of the line.

ignore_quiet_hours.description: `true` when the message was sent with `ignore_quiet_hours: true` on a line that is not a shared line: quiet hours do not hold it. `false` otherwise, on a shared line, on an inbound message and on a message typed on the device of the line. Set when the message is accepted and never changed after that.

queue_position.description: 0 when the message leaves immediately. Otherwise the rank of the message among the line's held messages, starting at 1.

is_new_contact.description: `true` when the recipient is a new contact for the line: that number has not written to the line in the last 30 days, which is the default length of that period. `false` when the recipient is a known contact.

daily_new_contacts_used.description: Distinct new contacts counted for the line in the last 24 hours, once this request is accepted.

daily_new_contact_limit.description: The line's limit of distinct new contacts per rolling 24 hours.

daily_known_contacts_used.description: Distinct known contacts counted for the line in the last 24 hours, once this request is accepted.

daily_known_contact_limit.description: The line's limit of distinct known contacts per rolling 24 hours.

daily_messages_used.description: Messages counted for the line in the last 24 hours, once this request is accepted. A held message counts when it is released, not when it is accepted.

daily_total_message_limit.description: The line's limit of messages per rolling 24 hours.

reply_lane.description: The same value as `reply_lane` of the message.

daily_replies_used.description: Reply-lane messages counted for the line in the last 24 hours, once this request is accepted.

daily_reply_limit.description: The line's limit of reply-lane messages per rolling 24 hours.

messages_ahead_in_queue.description: Number of held messages of the line planned to leave before this one. Present only when the message is held.

daily_slot_of.description: Date of the planned departure in the recipient's local time, as `YYYY-MM-DD`. Present only when iSnap placed the held message at a time in the line's sending hours.

target_activity_hour.description: Hour of the planned departure in the recipient's local time, 0 to 23. Present only with `daily_slot_of`.

next_slot_available_at.description: The planned departure time: the same value as `scheduled_for` of the message. Present only when the message is held.

last_new_contact_sent_at.description: When the line last sent a first message to a new contact. Present only when `schedule_reason` is `inter_new_contact_delay`.

min_inter_new_contact_seconds.description: The line's minimum number of seconds between two first messages to new contacts. Present only when `schedule_reason` is `inter_new_contact_delay`.

jitter_applied_seconds.description: Random number of seconds added to that minimum for this message. Present only when `schedule_reason` is `inter_new_contact_delay`.

queue_info.description: The state of the line's sending limits when the message was accepted. Filled only in the response of `POST /v1/messages` to a new request: `null` on every read, in the response to a retry with the same `Idempotency-Key`, and in events.

created_at.description: When iSnap recorded the message. On an inbound message it can be later than `delivered_at`, when the line's device was offline.

queued_at.description: When an outbound message entered the queue. `null` on an inbound message and on a message typed on the device of the line.

sent_at.description: When the line's device confirmed that it sent the message. `null` until then, and on an inbound message.

delivered_at.description: On an outbound message, the delivery time the line's device reported: `null` until it reports one. On an inbound message, the time the device received the message.

read_at.description: On an outbound message, the time the line's device reported that the recipient read it. On an inbound message, the time it was marked as read with `POST /v1/chats/{chat_id}/read`. `null` until then.

failed_at.description: When the message became `failed`. `null` otherwise. When the device of an iMessage line reports a failure after `sent`, `failed_at` holds the time of the send, not the time of the failure.

error_code.description: `null` unless the message is `failed`. When iSnap failed the message itself: `carrier_unavailable` (the message waited 48 hours without reaching a device), `no_terminal_ack` (the line's device took the message and never reported an outcome) or `carrier_terminated` (the line was terminated while the message was waiting). `null` when the line's device reported the failure: read `error_message`.

error_message.description: `null` unless the message is `failed`. A text that describes the failure. When the line's device reported the failure, it is the text the device gave, or `null` when it gave none.

cancelled_at.description: When the message was canceled. `null` otherwise.

MessageV1.description: A message sent or received by a line. The response of `POST /v1/messages`, the reads, the list items, the cancel response and the `message` field of the `message.*` events all carry this object. It has no chat id: the chat id is given by `GET /v1/chats` and by events. It carries personal data: the handles in `to` and `from`, the text in `body`, the file names of `attachments`, and what you put in `metadata`. Timestamps are ISO 8601 in UTC.

MessageDirection.description: `outbound`: a message the line sent, through the API or typed on the line's device. `inbound`: a message the line received.

MessageKind.description: `message`: a message with text, attachments or both. `voice`: a voice note. `reaction`: a reaction, recorded as its own entry.

MessageChannel.description: `auto` on a message sent through the API. On an inbound message and on a message typed on the line's device, the same value as `service`. `iMessage` on a reaction.

MessageService.description: The service the line's device reports it used: `iMessage`, `SMS` or `RCS`. On an outbound message it is `null` until the device confirms the send, and it stays `null` when the send fails or when the device does not report the service. On an inbound message, the service the message arrived on.

MessageStatus.description: `queued`: accepted and waiting for the line's device, or with the device, which has not reported the outcome. `scheduled`: held by iSnap until `scheduled_for`. `sent`: the device reported that it sent the message. `delivered`: the device reported a delivery receipt; every inbound message, and every message typed on the line's device, is `delivered` from the start. `read`: the device reported that the recipient read an outbound message. `failed`: the message failed, or iSnap stopped waiting for its outcome (`error_code: no_terminal_ack`), in which case it can have reached the recipient. iSnap never resends it. `cancelled`: canceled with `DELETE /v1/messages/{id}` before the device took it. An outbound message moves from `scheduled` to `queued`, `sent`, `delivered` and `read`, and no status is guaranteed to follow `sent`, `delivered` or `read`. On an iMessage line, a message sent over SMS or RCS gets no `delivered` and no `read`, and a `failed` can still follow its `sent`. `failed` can follow any status except `cancelled`, including `delivered` and `read`. `cancelled` is final. Treat `failed` as final: a send confirmation that arrives after a failure reported by the device sets `status` back to `sent` while `failed_at` stays set. A delivery receipt can arrive before the device confirms the send, and `status` then returns to `sent` while `delivered_at` stays set: read the timestamps, not only `status`.

id.description: Attachment id: `att_` followed by 25 letters or digits. Read the file with `GET /v1/attachments/{id}`.

content_type.description: Content type of the file, as declared when the attachment was created. `audio/x-caf` for an audio file that iSnap converted.

filename.description: File name. It can carry personal data.

size_bytes.description: Size in bytes, as declared when the attachment was created. For an audio file that iSnap converted, the size after conversion.

duration_ms.description: Duration in milliseconds of an audio file that iSnap converted. `null` on every other file.

MessageAttachmentV1.description: A file of a message. It carries no download URL: call `GET /v1/attachments/{id}` to get one.

reaction_type.description: `love`, `like`, `dislike`, `laugh`, `emphasize` or `question`, or `custom` for an emoji reaction from the contact.

reaction_emoji.description: The emoji of the reaction. For `custom`, the emoji the contact used, or `null` when the line's device did not report it.

from_handle.description: Handle of the author of the reaction: the contact's handle when `direction` is `inbound`, the line's number when it is `outbound`. A contact's handle is personal data.

direction.description: `outbound`: the line's own reaction. `inbound`: a reaction from the contact.

MessageReactionV1.description: A reaction on a message. A message carries at most one reaction per author.

trace_id.description: Trace id of the request that produced this response: 32 lowercase hexadecimal characters. Quote it when you report a problem to iSnap.

request_id.description: Id of the request that produced this response: `req_` followed by 25 letters or digits.

id.description: Id of the reaction: `msg_` followed by 25 letters or digits. `GET /v1/messages` lists the reaction as an entry whose `kind` is `reaction`.

parent_message_id.description: Id of the message the reaction is on.

type.description: The line's reaction on the message.

direction.description: Always `outbound` here: the line's own reaction.

status.description: `queued`: accepted, and the line's device has not confirmed it. `sent`: the device confirmed the reaction. `failed`: the device reported a failure, and the reaction stays in `reactions` of the message until you remove it.

Reaction.description: The line's reaction on a message, as accepted by `POST /v1/messages/{id}/reactions`.

type.description: The reaction to put on the message. It replaces the line's reaction on that message when there is one.

trace_id.description: Trace id of the request that produced this response: 32 lowercase hexadecimal characters. Quote it when you report a problem to iSnap.

request_id.description: Id of the request that produced this response: `req_` followed by 25 letters or digits.

removed.description: `true` when the line had a reaction on the message and its removal was accepted: it does not mean that the line's device removed it. `false` when the line had no reaction on the message.

type.description: The reaction that was removed. `null` when `removed` is `false`.

trace_id.description: Trace id of the request that produced this response: 32 lowercase hexadecimal characters. Quote it when you report a problem to iSnap.

request_id.description: Id of the request that produced this response: `req_` followed by 25 letters or digits.

next_cursor.description: Pass it as `cursor` to get the next page. `null` on the last page.

id.description: Id of the webhook subscription: `wh_` followed by 25 letters or digits.

events.description: Event filter: an array of exact event types, family wildcards such as `line.*`, or `*`. Never `null`.

A per-line subscription of yours for the line is canceled immediately, with a prorated credit, whatever the receiving account. When an `active` rented line goes to a direct account, that account must have a payment method on file, and it is charged immediately for a new per-line subscription; when that charge is declined, nothing moves. A BYOD line, or a rented line that is not `active`, goes to a direct account with no charge. A shared line, a test line or a dedicated pool line can go to a wholesale partner only.

The line keeps its id, its phone number, its `status`, its variant, its `metadata` and its chats. The receiving account lists those chats, with their `contact_handle`, and can receive your unread inbound messages of those chats and the events about the messages you sent on the line: export what you need from those chats before the transfer. The `anniversary_at`, `billing_anchor_at`, `cancel_at` and `pending_variant` of the line are cleared, so a scheduled end is dropped; a wholesale partner that receives the line gets a new `anniversary_at` and a new `activated_at`, both set to the time of the transfer.

By default the device of the line stays connected, and the line keeps working for its new owner. This operation sends no event to either account; later events about the line go to its new owner.

post.description:
Moves a rented line you own between the inbound-only variant (`inbound_only: true`) and the two-way variant (`inbound_only: false`), keeping its phone number. Accepts an API key. The line must be an `active` rented line with no per-line subscription.

While no change is pending, asking for the value the line already has returns `200` and stores nothing, so the response carries `pending_variant: null`. Resending the pending change returns it unchanged. Any other scheduled request while a change is pending returns `409 variant_change_already_pending`, even for the value the line already has. An immediate change does not clear a pending one. At its date, a scheduled change is dropped, with no event, when the line is `suspended`, is no longer a rented line, has a per-line subscription, or already has the scheduled value. A line that has ended keeps its `pending_variant`, and the change never applies.

Events: `line.variant_changed` when a change applies, with `scheduled: false` for an immediate change and `true` for a scheduled one, and `line.variant_scheduled` when a change is scheduled.

post.description:
Commits a draft pre-order. Accepts an API key. A line-scoped key is not limited to its list on this operation: it can confirm any draft of the account. The confirmation sends no event: iSnap sends `pre_order.fulfilled`, which carries the `line_id`, when the line is handed over.

The build of a pre-order sets `status` to `provisioning` and `estimated_fulfillment` to the time the build starts plus 72 hours, and creates on your account a rented iMessage line with `status: provisioning`, with the `inbound_only` and the `billing_anchor_at` of the pre-order. When a number is in stock in one of your area codes, in their order of preference, it is assigned to the line when the build starts. A pre-order with no `preferred_area_codes` takes any number in stock.

For a wholesale partner the build starts with the confirmation. A wholesale partner pays nothing at confirmation: `stripe_client_secret` is `null`, and the line is billed on the monthly invoice from the day it is handed over.

For a direct account the build starts when the first month is paid. Confirm starts a monthly subscription, sets `status` to `awaiting_payment` and returns `stripe_client_secret`, a client secret that your payment page passes to the payment form of Stripe to collect the first month. Only card payments are accepted. Until that payment succeeds, no line is created and `estimated_fulfillment` is `null`. After paying, read the pre-order with `GET /v1/pre-orders/{id}` until `status` is `provisioning`. When the first month is not paid within 23 hours of the confirmation, `status` becomes `cancelled` and iSnap sends `pre_order.cancelled`. When a credit balance of the account at Stripe covers the first month, there is nothing to pay: the build starts with the confirmation and `stripe_client_secret` is `null`. The first month starts at the confirmation, not when the line is handed over, and the next invoice is issued one month after the confirmation. The hand-over of the line takes no payment and does not change when the subscription is invoiced.

Confirm can be repeated while `status` is `awaiting_payment`: it returns the same client secret and starts no second subscription. Repeated after the payment succeeded, it returns the pre-order in `provisioning`.

Any other pre-order returns `400 pre_order_not_draft`, including one that was canceled because its first month was not paid in time. A confirmation that runs at the same time as a cancellation, or for a wholesale partner as another confirmation, returns `409 pre_order_not_draft`. When Stripe cannot be reached, the call returns `503 payment_provider_unavailable`: nothing changed, and the call can be repeated. When Stripe refuses the request for the account, the call returns `409 payment_setup_failed`: nothing changed, and repeating the call does not help. Once its build has started, a pre-order cannot be canceled through the API.

Accepts one message to one phone number on one of your lines. Returns `202` with the message as `queued`, or as `scheduled` when iSnap holds it: `scheduled_for` is then the planned departure time and `schedule_reason` names the cause. A `202` means that the message is accepted, not that it is sent. The line's device chooses the service (`iMessage`, `RCS` or `SMS`) when it sends, and `service` then shows the one it used. Body fields the API does not know are ignored. `POST /v1/messages` and `GET /v1/messages` share 60 requests per 60 seconds per network address.

The message then produces events: `message.queued`, or `message.scheduled` while it is held and `message.queued` when it is released, then `message.sent` or `message.failed`. `message.delivered` and `message.read` follow only when the line's device reports them. `message.fallback_triggered` is sent when the device reports that the message went out, or was attempted, over SMS or RCS instead of iMessage.

Accepts an API key or a trial key. An API key that starts with `isnap_test_` sends real messages, like one that starts with `isnap_live_`. A line-scoped key sends only on the lines in its `line_ids`. A trial key sends only from the trial's line to the phone number paired with the trial, text only: the sending limits and quiet hours do not apply to it, and it returns `402 trial_needs_inbound` while the trial is `dormant`.

Send an `Idempotency-Key` header to make a retry safe (`X-Idempotency-Key` is read when it is absent). A retry with the same key and the same body on the same line sends nothing and returns `202` with the existing message in its current state, with `queue_info` set to `null`. The same key with a different body returns `409 idempotency_conflict`. A key that the line already used for a reaction call returns `202` with that reaction entry, and the message is not sent: use a new key for every action. iSnap remembers a key for as long as its message exists, which is at least 72 hours. Keep the key at 255 characters or fewer: a longer key returns `500 internal_error`. Send retries one after the other: of two simultaneous requests with the same new key, one is accepted and the other is either replayed or returns `500 internal_error`.

On a shared line, the first message to a contact returns `503 line_pool_exhausted` when no phone number is available to serve that contact, and `503 quota_state_unavailable` when that availability could not be read: retry the request.

The response carries personal data: the handles in `to` and `from`, the text in `body`, the file names of the attachments and your `metadata`.

line_id.description: The line that sends the message: `line_` followed by 25 letters or digits. It must be a line of your account whose status is `active`.

to.description: Recipient phone number, 1 to 30 characters. E.164 is preferred; a number without a country code is read as a US number. iSnap normalizes it to E.164 and returns the normalized value in `to` of the message. An email address or an Apple ID returns `400 bad_request`, even when `POST /v1/lookup` reports that it can receive iMessage. One request has one recipient: there is no group send.

A line has at most one reaction per message: a request with another `type` replaces it, and a request with the `type` already in place changes nothing and returns the existing reaction, even when its `status` is `failed`. To try a failed reaction again, remove it, then add it again.

Returns `202`: the reaction is handed to the line's device like a message. `reaction.added` is sent when the device confirms it. If the device reports a failure, no event is sent and the reaction's `status` becomes `failed`. If the line has no paired device, the reaction stays `queued` and no event follows. The `reactions` list of the message shows the reaction as soon as this request is accepted, before the device confirms it, and keeps showing it when the device reports a failure.

The message must be an iMessage message that the line's device has confirmed, with at most one attachment, and the handle of its contact must be 20 characters or fewer, which every phone number is. For a message you sent, wait for `message.sent`. A message typed on the line's device itself is always refused with `422 parent_not_yet_acked`. The line must be `active`.

The key shares the line's keys with `POST /v1/messages`, and the reverse does not conflict: a `POST /v1/messages` whose key the line already used for a reaction returns `202` with that reaction entry and sends no message. Creates a webhook subscription: iSnap sends the events that match `events` and `line_ids` to `url`, as an HTTPS `POST` with a JSON body. Accepts an API key; a line-scoped key is not restricted here and can subscribe to every line of the account. The signing secret is returned in this response only. The operation is not idempotent: the same request sent twice creates two subscriptions, and each event is then delivered twice to the URL. There is no limit on the number of subscriptions. `description` and `active` are ignored on create: set them with `PATCH /v1/webhooks/{id}`. Creating a subscription sends no event.

After 10 consecutive deliveries that used all their attempts, iSnap suspends the subscription: it then sends a signed `webhook.test` request at most once every 15 minutes, and a response from `200` to `299` within 10 seconds resumes the subscription. A suspended subscription still reads `active: true`, and no operation resumes it. Events that occur while a subscription is suspended or inactive are not recorded for it and are not delivered later. The URL is checked again before every attempt and every probe: when its host then resolves to a non-public address, no request is sent and the subscription is suspended immediately.

A delivery succeeds when the URL returns a status from `200` to `299` within 10 seconds; redirects are not followed and `Retry-After` is ignored. Any other outcome is a failed attempt. A retry schedule has at most 7 attempts: the first immediately, then 30 seconds, 1 minute, 5 minutes, 30 minutes, 2 hours and 12 hours after the previous attempt, which adds up to 14 hours 36 minutes 30 seconds. A delivery that iSnap resends after a suspension or a stall starts a new schedule. A `410` response is not retried and sets `active` to `false`. Delivery order is not guaranteed, and an event can be delivered more than once: deduplicate on `event_id`.

Each request is signed according to Standard Webhooks, with three headers: `webhook-id` (the `event_id` of the event, the same on every attempt and on a replay), `webhook-timestamp` (the time the attempt is sent, in Unix seconds) and `webhook-signature` (`v1,` followed by the base64 HMAC-SHA256 of `<webhook-id>.<webhook-timestamp>.<body>`, computed on the body exactly as sent). The headers `X-iSnap-Event` (the event type), `X-iSnap-Delivery-Id` (the delivery id) and `X-iSnap-Attempt` (the attempt number, from 1) are informational and not signed. `X-iSnap-Webhook-Id` holds an opaque value that is not the `id` of the subscription.

A chat belongs to its line, not to an account: after a line changes owner, by a transfer or by a return to the marketplace, the account that owns the line lists its chats, those of earlier owners included, and the earlier owner no longer sees them. When the new owner marks one of these chats read, it receives in `message.read` the inbound messages of the earlier owner that iSnap still keeps and that were not marked read. Before you transfer a line or let it return to the marketplace, export what you need from its chats. Filter with `line_id`, `since` and `until`. The response carries `items`, `has_more` and `next_cursor`: pass `next_cursor` as `cursor` to get the next page, and stop when `has_more` is `false`: `next_cursor` is then `null`. A malformed `cursor` is not an error: the list restarts from the first page, and nothing in the response says so. Chats move during a walk: a chat that has a new message moves to the front of the list, before the cursor, and the walk does not return it, and a message that the device reports late can move a chat back, so that the walk returns it twice. Deduplicate on `id`, then list again with `since` set earlier than the start of your walk by the reporting delay that you accept. Accepts an API key. A line-scoped key lists only the chats of the lines in its `line_ids`. `contact_handle` is personal data.

post.description:
Builds a contact card, which is a vCard 3.0 file, from the fields of the request and sends it to the chat's contact as a message with one attachment, on the chat's line. The message is sent like a message of `POST /v1/messages`: it counts against the line's sending limits, iSnap can hold it, and it produces the same `message.*` events. The handle of the chat's contact must be a phone number.

Returns `202` with `message_id`, `attachment_id` and `status`. `status` always reads `queued`, even when iSnap holds the message: read the message with `GET /v1/messages/{id}` to know its `status`. The response carries no `X-iSnap-Quota-*` headers. `first_name` is required, with at least one of `phone_numbers`, `emails` or a non-empty `organization`. When `avatar_url` cannot be fetched, the API returns `502 avatar_fetch_failed` and nothing is sent.

The API cannot replay this call. Once a call has created the message, a repeat with the same `Idempotency-Key` returns `409 idempotency_conflict` instead of the first result. A repeat of a call that failed before the message was created, for example on a `429` or on `502 avatar_fetch_failed`, sends the card. Do not retry this call automatically: after an error, check with `GET /v1/messages` whether the first call created the message. On a shared line, the call returns `503 line_pool_exhausted` when no phone number is available to serve the contact, and `503 quota_state_unavailable` when that availability could not be read: retry the request.

Accepts an API key. A line-scoped key gets `403 forbidden` when the chat's line is outside its `line_ids`. The fields of the card are personal data of the person they describe: iSnap stores them in the attachment it creates.

post.description:
Starts a trial: a prospect exchanges messages between their own phone and an iSnap line, and you send and read the messages of the trial with a trial key. Accepts an API key. A line-scoped key is not limited to its list on this operation. Returns `token`, a 7-character pairing code: the prospect sends a message that contains it to `pool_line_number` within 15 minutes (`pairing_expires_at`). The code is matched case-insensitively, as a word of its own. When it matches, the trial becomes `active`, iSnap sends `trial.linked`, and the prospect receives one confirmation message. Starting a trial sends no event.

The trial key is not in this response: read it once with `GET /v1/trial/status` after pairing. It sends only from the line of the trial and only to the handle of the prospect, and every message it sends ends with your `footer`, or with the footer of iSnap. A trial that is `active` or `dormant` lasts until it is revoked.

Every field of the body is optional, and a request without a body is valid; a key that is not listed returns `400 validation_failed`. An account that is not a wholesale partner can have one trial at a time that is `active`, `dormant`, or `pairing_pending` with its pairing window still open: another call returns `409 trial_already_active`. A `pairing_pending` trial whose pairing window ended does not count. A wholesale partner can start any number of trials. `Idempotency-Key` is ignored: a repeated call starts another trial for a wholesale partner. Returns `503 line_pool_exhausted` when no line is available for a trial, and `503 pairing_code_unavailable` when iSnap could not draw a new pairing code: repeat the call.

This read changes the trial: the first call after pairing returns the trial key once, and a call made after the pairing window ended without a pairing revokes the trial. Call it only from the backend that stores the key, and never retry it automatically. Returns the state of a trial from its pairing code. Needs no credential: `token`, the pairing code that the prospect sees and types, is the only input. `status` is `pairing_pending`, `active` or `dormant`. After pairing, the first call returns `trial_api_key` once, and later calls omit it. The key can be read that first time for 1 hour after the pairing: after that hour it is never returned and the trial cannot send, so revoke the trial and start another. Whoever calls first after the pairing receives the key: call from your backend as soon as `trial.linked` arrives.

Returns `410 pairing_expired` for a revoked trial, whatever the reason of the revoke, and for a trial whose pairing window ended without a pairing: that call also revokes the trial, and no event is sent. Returns `404 trial_not_found` when no trial has this code. `paired_handle` is personal data.

post.description:
Issues a single-use activation code, valid 5 minutes, with the download links of the bridge app. Accepts an API key. A line-scoped key is not limited to its list on this operation: each code it issues can create a line. The user installs the bridge app on their Mac, paired with their iPhone, or on their Android phone, and enters the code. That creates a new BYOD line on your account, with `status: active`, and iSnap sends `line.connected`. The app decides the platform: a Mac gives an iMessage line, an Android phone an Android line. The `phone_number` of the line is empty until the line's device reports it; no event announces it, so read the line. Issuing a code sends no event.

An account that is not a wholesale partner needs a free BYOD slot, and no operation that an API key can call buys one. The call returns `402 payment_required` when the account has no BYOD slot, and `404 no_slot_available` when every slot is used by a line that is not terminated. A wholesale partner needs no slot. The slot is checked when the code is issued, not when it is used, and a code reserves no slot.

Every call issues another code, and `Idempotency-Key` is ignored. Each pairing creates a new line: no operation moves a BYOD line to another device. End a BYOD line with `POST /v1/lines/{id}/terminate`, which frees its slot. The body accepts `metadata` only: any other key returns `400 validation_failed`.

post.description:
Rents one hosted macOS session from the stock of iSnap. Wholesale partners only: any other account is refused with `403 not_a_wholesale_partner`, and no other operation that an API key can call rents a session. Accepts an API key. A line-scoped key is not limited to its list on this operation. A hosted macOS session is a macOS user account on a Mac that iSnap hosts, signed in to no Apple ID when you receive it. It is not a line: it has no number and sends nothing. It runs the bridge app of a BYOD line. The rental starts immediately and `anniversary_at` is set to the time of the call: the session is billed every month on that day of the month, at that time of day, in UTC; in a shorter month, on its last day.

Returns `409 no_macos_session_in_stock` when no session is free. Nothing is recorded in that case; iSnap can assign a session to your account later, which `macos_session.rented` announces, and that assignment is not linked to the refused call. Send an `Idempotency-Key` header: without one, every call rents another billable session, a retry included.

You can rent any number of sessions; on the monthly invoice, the sessions beyond your number of BYOD lines are also billed as BYOD lines. The body is optional and accepts `metadata` only. The rent call itself sends no event: `macos_session.rented` is sent only when iSnap assigns a session without a rent call. No operation lists sessions: keep the `id` from this response or from the event.

schema.description: Optional key that makes a retry safe. A request repeated with the same key, by the same API key, with the same method, path and body, within 24 hours, returns the first successful response unchanged, its `trace_id` and `request_id` included, and does not act again. The body is compared byte for byte: a request with no body and a request with `{}` are two different requests. The same key with another method, path or body returns `409 idempotency_key_collision`. While the first request is still running, a retry returns `503 idempotency_in_flight`; a request that never completes frees its key after 60 seconds. Only a `2xx` response is recorded: after a failed request, the retry runs again. At most 255 characters: a longer key returns `400 validation_failed`. The `X-Idempotency-Key` header is read when `Idempotency-Key` is absent.

post.summary: Cancel a hosted macOS session at its next anniversary
post.description:
Schedules the end of the rental of a hosted macOS session at its next anniversary. Accepts an API key. A line-scoped key is not limited to its list on this operation. Sets `cancel_at` to the next occurrence of `anniversary_at`, day and time, strictly after the call: a cancel sent on the anniversary day after the time of `anniversary_at` ends the rental one month later, and one sent earlier that day ends it the same day. The session works and is billed until `cancel_at`. A second call returns the same `cancel_at`. Only the account that rents the session can cancel it: any other account gets `404 macos_session_not_found`. The cancel call itself sends no event.

After `cancel_at`, iSnap releases the session. The API does not bound the delay between `cancel_at` and the release. At release, the metadata of the rental is cleared, iSnap sends `macos_session.released` with `reason: cancelled`, and every later operation on the session returns `404`. If the session runs the bridge app of one of your BYOD lines, that bridge app is stopped and iSnap sends `line.disconnected` with `reason: scheduled_cancellation` for the line.
